newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan naphtha sales hit record high for March.
newsitem.headline: Japan naphtha sales hit record high for March.

text.p: Domestic sales of naphtha in March hit record highs for the month, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.

Deliveries of naphtha climbed 18.4 percent over year-earlier levels to 4.28 million kilolitres (868,000 barrels per day), mainly on the back of surging petrochemical needs to produce ethylene and aromatics, MITI said.
Japan's ethylene output in March totalled 631,000 tonnes, up 14.2 percent from a year earlier, as fewer ethylene plants were closed for routine maintenance this year.
Demand for kerosene and fuel oil A, both used for heating purposes in Japan, fell because of milder than usual temperatures in March.
Average temperatures were 1.2 degrees Celsius higher in March compared with a year earlier.
Kerosene sales fell 19.4 percent year-on-year to 3.07 million kl (623,000 barrels per day), while those of fuel oil A fell 7.9 percent to 2.77 million kl (562,000 barrels per day).
